newsitem.title: GREECE: GNN MACRO GUIDE: TAXATION SYSTEMS.
newsitem.headline: GNN MACRO GUIDE: TAXATION SYSTEMS.

text.p: A brief description of the main taxation systems follows:

PRORTIONAL TAX SYSTEM: As personal income goes up, the tax bill goes up in exactly the same proportion (FLAT RATE TAX). In other words, taxpayers at all income levels end up paying the same proportion of their income in taxes.
The average tax rate is equal to the marginal tax rate.
Average tax rate= Total tax divided by total income
PROGRESSIVE TAX SYSTEM: As a person's income rises, the proportion of income paid in taxes rises.
The average tax rate is less than the marginal tax rate. REGRESSIVE TAX SYSTEM: A smaller proportion of income is taken in taxes as income goes up.
The average tax rate exceeds the marginal tax rate. THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT CRITERIA FOR TAX FAIRNESS: 1) HORIZONTAL EQUITY
Equal income is taxed equally no matter how it is earned. (The same amount of money earned by a blue-collar worker and a gambler should be treated the same way.) 2) VERTICAL EQUITY
Unequal income is treated unequally. High income earners and low income earners should be treated differently.
Critics argue that it is difficult to judge how much
greater is one person's ability to pay than someone else's.
People should be taxed in proportion to the benefits they

receive from government services.( user taxes, tolls, gasoline tax is partly based on this principle). But it is difficult to be applied and critics argue that taxes paid bear little resemblance to the payments individuals receive. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
